title: Scout P6-S1 (review path at Phase I code, READ wt/goal-T-0445): how reviews are spawned and tiered, what the review prompt and packet contain now, what a review row and result record (verdict, comments, severities), how two-review tasks are handled, and what historical review data exists to measure defect detection by packet version
spec:
Read-only. Work in /Users/k3ntaw/code/orchestrator/wt/goal-T-0445 (Phase I head 4149f67). Program: .orchestrator/phase-i-program.md section P6. Deliver, each item with path:line:
1. Review spawning: daemon._open_reviews / reviews_expected / merge_reviewed: when one vs two reviews fire ([review] two_reviews_from, direct_merge_max, security_paths, semantic triggers, SECURITY_CHECKLIST_COMPLEXITY bump), which tier and account each review gets (review_tier, security_review_tier, avoid executor account), how verdicts are bucketed and how request_changes holds the task; the adversarial-review skill and .orchestrator/prompts/review.md contents after P1b (review_packet sections, security section conditions, the checklist reference .claude/skills/adversarial-review/references/security-checklist.md).
2. Review results: the exact shape bus.post_result stores for a review (verdict, comments with path/line/severity/issue, summary, confidence), what spawn.run_worker logs on the review run row (role review, tier, usd, tokens, packet_meta after P1b), and whether the reviewed sha and packet version are recorded (G8 review binding, H8 header).
3. Historical data: over .orchestrator/tasks/*.json count review tasks by verdict, comments per review, severity distribution, and how many tasks had two reviews; list the fields available to compute "defects found per review" and "distinct defects across the two reviews of one task" (overlap by path+line or issue text); say what is missing to compare findings before and after the P1b packet (packet_meta.version on review rows exists from when?).
4. Where a reviewer role label would attach (spawn.run_worker render kwargs, prompts) so two reviews of one task can receive different role prompts (A: acceptance, correctness, regressions, tests; B: adversarial, security, edge cases, hidden assumptions) without changing the security checklist path.
5. Existing tests pinning review spawning and verdict handling (tests/test_daemon.py, tests/test_spawn.py).
Output under 1,500 tokens, confidence per section, provenance repo.
acceptance: review spawning rules, tiers, checklist bump and verdict bucketing with path:line
review result shape and review run-row fields listed, with whether reviewed sha and packet version are recorded
historical counts: reviews by verdict, comments per review, severity distribution, two-review tasks, and the fields for defect and overlap metrics
the attachment point for a reviewer role label and the pinning tests listed

reviews_expected(t): 1 if orphaned or complexity<TWO_REVIEWS_FROM(default 7 from pool.toml [review].two_reviews_from), else 2

_review_plan(t) is the real source of truth gate() uses: orphaned->1("orphaned"); CODE_REVIEW=never->0; security_paths mode-> 0 or 1 depending on security/semantic path or pattern match, failing closed to 1 on diff_unavailable/security_paths_empty; always mode-> 0 if complexity<=DIRECT_MERGE_MAX(default 3) else reviews_expected(t)

review_tier(t): claude:sonnet executor -> opus review; claude:opus executor -> sonnet review; else default sonnet (never self-review). _security_review_tier(t) uses SECURITY_REVIEW_TIER (default sonnet) unless executor is that same claude tier, then the other tier

_open_reviews creates n_reviews review tasks: security reviews force complexity=max(complexity,SECURITY_CHECKLIST_COMPLEXITY=7) and tier=_security_review_tier; second non-security review of a Claude-executed task also uses review_tier(t) again, otherwise it uses _other_tier(existing[0]['tier']) so the two reviews land on different tiers; each review task inherits reviewed_sha and is filtered to only count reviews matching the current head sha

Verdict bucketing in _merge_reviewed_one: done reviews classified via failures._review_verdict (review's own review_verdict/result.verdict first, src fallback only if single review); anything not 'approve' is 'rejected' -> immediately holds the source task with hold_reason 'review request_changes: <id> (<verdict>)', without waiting for the sibling review

merge only fires once len(approved)>=needed(reviews_expected stamped on pipeline at gate time, not re-derived); still-pending siblings block merge but don't hold; failed/held reviews (stuck) hold the source with a distinct reason

adversarial-review SKILL.md: reviewer sees -U3 hunks only, reads a single path only if ambiguous; complexity>=7 triggers references/security-checklist.md; must return ONLY {verdict, comments[{path,line,issue,severity}]} via bus_post_result — no summary/confidence field in the contract
.orchestrator/prompts/review.md (post-P1b) is just {{packet}} + fixed instructions; no separate role-prompt scaffolding beyond the packet content

review_packet(task,reviewed) sections: spec, acceptance, scope, (diff placeholder), changed tests (present/missing per acceptance test id + changed test files), gate (gated_at/attempts/reds/first_green/last_failure_head); security section appended when a security glob matches scope, a semantic regex (auth|credential|secret|token|permission|crypt|security) hits spec+diff, complexity>=SECURITY_CHECKLIST_COMPLEXITY, or review_reason is security_paths/diff_unavailable/security_paths_empty — pointing at 'checklist: skills/review/adversarial-review/references/security-checklist.md' (not .claude/skills/... as the task assumed); fix-round context section appended when constraints.fix_round_for is set

bus.post_result for review stores fit_result({'summary':result.get('summary',''), **result}) where result=extract_json(model text) — i.e. verdict, comments (each {path,line,issue,severity}), plus whatever else the model returned; no 'confidence' field is part of the review schema (that only exists for spec_review's 'risks' and for challenge/scout outputs)
